Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.
Go to Settings → Pages in your GitHub repo Set Source to Deploy from a branch Set Branch to gh-pages / / (root) Push to main — your site deploys automatically

A repository other than .github.io is published at https:// .github.io/ /, under a path prefix. --base-path auto in the workflow above handles it: in GitHub Actions it reads the repository name, so every asset, page, link, search and Markdown URL starts with /, and the sitemap, llms.txt and canonical links use https:// .github.io/ as the site URL. Nothing else to configure, and no custom domain needed. auto builds for the root when the repository has a CNAME file, when the repository is .github.io, when seo.siteUrl is set (its path is the prefix), and outside GitHub Actions. To set the prefix yourself: The same works for any host that serves the site under a path, such as example.com/docs behind a reverse proxy (--base-path /docs). Write links in your Markdown as usual (/docs/guide, ../img/x.png): the build and the app add the prefix. Order of precedence: --base-path, then site.basePath, then the path of seo.siteUrl. --base-path / builds for the root. If you deploy with actions/configure-pages (Pages source "GitHub Actions"), you can pass its output instead, which also knows a custom domain set in the repository settings: --base-path "${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}". Preview a prefixed build locally: aiui serve --base-path /my-repo serves it at http://127.0.0.1:8000/my-repo/ (and aiui serve --no-build serves an existing build under the prefix it was built for). Under a prefix, the legacy plugins that read the URL themselves (content-loader, homepage, topnav) are not supported; the default nav-intercept and fetch-retry are.

To use a custom domain (e.g., docs.example.com): Create a CNAME file in your repo root: Configure DNS — add a CNAME record pointing to .github.io The workflow above copies CNAME into the build output. The build also uses it as the site URL for the sitemap and canonical links.

MkDocs AIUI mkdocs.yml aiui.yaml mkdocs build → ./site/ aiui build --output site → ./site/ mkdocs serve aiui dev pip install mkdocs-material pip install aiui What carries over from Material for MkDocs pages: Admonitions (!!! note "Title", collapsible ???), content tabs (=== "Tab" with 4-space indented content) and fenced code blocks render. attr_list ({ .class }) is not supported and shows as literal text; :material-*: icon shortcodes do not render as icons; raw HTML blocks are not styled. Remove them. The nav: list in mkdocs.yml is not read. Pages are ordered by the frontmatter order value, then a number prefix in the file name (01-intro.md), then the file name. See Navigation.

Create aiui.yaml (see the example above) and run aiui validate --strict. Replace mkdocs build with aiui build --output site --minify in your CI workflow. Check the pages for the unsupported syntax listed above. Push to main.

aiui build --output site produces: With a site URL (seo.siteUrl, or the CNAME file) the build also writes sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt; see SEO. Everything is static, so GitHub Pages serves it directly.

Opening a page from the sidebar fetches its .md file. A reader on a lossy network (Wi-Fi, VPN, a mobile link) sometimes gets one new connection that hangs for 15 to 30 seconds while every other request is fast. The docs app keeps one such request from freezing the page: Time limit and retry. Each request for a page has 5 seconds to get an answer from the server. Past that it is cancelled and a fresh request goes out, which opens a new connection. There are three attempts (5 s, 5 s, then 10 s for a link that is only slow), with a short random pause between them. A network error or a 5xx answer is retried the same way; a 404 is not. Stalled downloads. Once the answer starts, a page whose download sends nothing for 5 seconds has stalled and is requested again; one that keeps arriving, however slowly, gets up to 15 seconds. Prefetch. Resting the pointer on a sidebar, previous / next or in-article docs link for 80 ms, focusing it with the keyboard, or pressing it starts loading that page. Once a page has shown, its previous and next pages load while the browser is idle. In-memory cache. A page loaded or prefetched once shows at once when you come back to it, without a request, until the tab is reloaded. The last click wins. Clicking another link cancels the request for the page you left, so fast clicking never builds a queue. No long wait for the renderer. A fetched page waits at most one second for the code highlighter and math renderer; after that the text shows and upgrades when they arrive. Retry state. When every attempt fails, the page says "Couldn't load this page" with a Retry button instead of a loading skeleton. First load. Every page aiui build writes carries the navigation (docs-nav.json), the route manifest and the page's own Markdown, so a first visit asks for none of them; ui-config.json is preloaded with the page (a live aiui serve adds Ask AI, MCP and feedback to it, so it is not baked in). The loader's tag names the plugins, so plugins/plugins.json is not requested either: on this site a first docs page went from five JSON requests and three plugin scripts to one and two. A file the page does not carry (a navigation over 100 KB, the navigation of a site with sign-in, a page served without its content) loads with the same time limit and retries as a page. If it cannot load, the page says "Couldn't load the docs" with a Retry button instead of staying blank. This site, https://ui.praison.ai, is built the same way: see .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml.

The docs app renders code (Shiki), mermaid diagrams, MkDocs tabs and admonitions, "On this page" and the header tabs itself. By default a build loads only one of the vanilla plugins in plugins/: Plugin Why it loads nav-intercept Keeps in-article /docs links on in-app navigation (no full page load) fetch-retry (retry a failed request for the site manifests) is no longer in the default list: the app reads the navigation and route manifest from the page and fetches ui-config.json with its own time limit and retries, which fetch-retry leaves alone. List it under site.plugins to keep it. mermaid, syntax-highlight, code-copy, toc, mkdocs-compat, content-loader, homepage and topnav no longer load by default: they skip React docs pages, and mermaid and syntax-highlight fetched about 40 files from cdn.jsdelivr.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com on every page (each new origin is another connection that can stall). A site can still list any of them under site.plugins in aiui.yaml. index.html loads plugins/plugin-loader.js?v=, where the version is a hash of the plugin files in the build (also in plugins/plugins.json), and names the plugins on the same tag (data-plugins), so the loader does not fetch plugins.json (a server's pages, which lack it, still do). The loader imports every plugin with the same ?v=, so browsers and the CDN cache them until a build changes a plugin.
